handbook-cable-text: Cables join storage into one network. A cable links to every cable, terminal and storage block it touches; arms on the cable show what it is connected to. Storage counts when it touches a cable or a terminal's cable port. By default that is chests, trunks, reed baskets, storage vessels, labeled chests and crates. Server owners can add more storage types in the simplenetwork.json config file; look at a block and type /stn check to see whether it counts. Storage inside someone else's land claim, or padlocked by someone else, is skipped. Hiding cables: right-click a cable while holding a chiseled block to hide the cable inside it. The network still runs through, and you can keep chiseling the block. Breaking it gives you back both the chiseled block and the cable.
handbook-terminal-text: The terminal shows everything stored in its network. It connects through the cable ports on its top, bottom and back, and faces you when placed. Taking items: left-click takes a stack, right-click takes one, shift + left-click sends a stack straight to your inventory. Storing items: click the grid while holding items, or shift-click items in your inventory. Crafting: used-up ingredients are refilled from the network after each craft. Shift-click the output to keep crafting until your inventory is full or the ingredients run out. Recipes: switch the view to Recipes or Craftable, then click a recipe to fill the crafting grid with its ingredients.
handbook-wireless-text: Sneak + right-click a Network Terminal to link the wireless terminal to it. After that, right-click anywhere to open that terminal's network, as long as you are within range (64 blocks by default; server owners can change this with WirelessRange in simplenetwork.json). Everything works just like at the terminal itself, including crafting. Moving out of range closes the window.
handbook-importer-text:
Place the importer against any block with an inventory, such as a hopper, chest or a machine's output side, and connect a cable to its other sides. Every second it pulls a few items out of that block into the network. The block itself decides which slot gives up items, the same way it does for hoppers and chutes, so from a firepit you only get the finished output.

Right-click the importer with an item to only import that item; sneak + right-click with an empty hand to import everything again. The front (the coloured ring) is the side that faces the block.
handbook-exporter-text:
Place the exporter against a block with an inventory and connect a cable to its other sides. Right-click it with an item to choose what to send; every second it pushes a few of that item from the network into the block, for example firewood into a firepit. The block decides which slot it goes into, the same way it does for hoppers and chutes. Without a filter, the exporter does nothing.

Sneak + right-click with an empty hand to clear the filter. The front (the coloured ring) is the side that faces the block.
handbook-configurator-text: Sneak + right-click any network storage container with the configurator to open its settings. Priority (-10 to 10, default 0): containers with a higher priority are filled first, and items are taken from lower-priority containers first. Give your main chest a high priority to keep it stocked. Filter (up to 9 items): a container with a filter only accepts those items from the network. Containers whose filter names an item get it before unfiltered containers of the same priority. Items already inside are never moved out. Breaking a container clears its settings.
guide-text: SimpleNetwork lets you reach all of your storage from one place. 1. Craft cables and a terminal. One copper ingot makes four Network Cables. A Network Terminal is made from copper ingots, clear quartz and a cable. 2. Connect your storage. Run cables so they touch your chests, crates and vessels. Everything connected becomes one network. 3. Connect the terminal. Attach a cable to the terminal's top, bottom or back port. 4. Use it. Right-click the terminal to search, sort, take and store items, and to craft straight from your storage. 5. Go wireless (optional). Craft a Wireless Terminal, sneak + right-click your terminal to link it, and open your network from anywhere within range. 6. Automate (optional). A Network Importer pulls items from the block it faces into the network; a Network Exporter pushes a chosen item from the network into the block it faces. Use them to collect from hoppers or keep a firepit fuelled. 7. Organise (optional). With a Network Configurator, sneak + right-click a container to give it a priority or a filter, e.g. so ores always go into one particular chest.
